title: Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Premium Rating Rule
content:
**Rating rule.** The full-term Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage premium of a vehicle is the physical damage base premium on the vehicle's rating worksheet for the term, multiplied by the deductible option's deductible factor, and, when the loan/lease payoff option is carried, further multiplied by one plus the loan/lease payoff premium percentage; the result is rounded to the cent, half up.

This premium enters the base premium of the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, where surcharges and discounts are applied under that policy's premium rating, and every change to it during the term is prorated as additional or return premium on the auto policy.

While the vehicle is in storage its physical damage premium is the comprehensive share only, which is 40 percent of the full physical damage premium. Deductible Rewards carries no premium.

## Elements of the rule

| Element | Source of the figure |
|---|---|
| Physical damage base premium | The vehicle's rating worksheet for the policy and term |
| Deductible factor | The deductible option's rating factor |
| Loan/lease payoff loading | One plus the option's loan/lease payoff premium percentage, applied only when that option is carried |
| Rounding | To the cent, half up, on the final figure |
| Storage | 40 percent of the full physical damage premium |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A vehicle's rating worksheet shows a physical damage base premium of 800.00 for the term, and the vehicle carries the Cardinal Physical Damage $1,000 Deductible option (deductible factor 0.84).

- Without the loan/lease payoff option: 800.00 multiplied by 0.84 gives 672.00.
- With the loan/lease payoff option at 6 percent: 672.00 multiplied by 1.06 gives 712.32.
- Put in storage without the loan/lease payoff option: 40 percent of 672.00 gives 268.80.

Enrolling Deductible Rewards on this vehicle leaves every figure above unchanged.
